model_reported.summary: Proposed one isolated pure-scalar DFA variant while retaining the existing ASCII run fast path and input/output ABI.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: The candidate uses only portable byte tables and scalar control flow; it introduces no target-specific feature or additional threading.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: No compiler-, hardware-, or library-specific API is used; this experiment tests a standard scalar DFA design.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Recorded the valid three-sample baseline mean as the comparator and left candidate correctness and speed claims to controller measurement.

proposal.hypothesis: On mixed-width input, selecting widths and checking special lead-byte bounds through the baseline's scalar branch tree may cost more control flow than a compact state DFA. This pure-scalar candidate retains ASCII run skipping and uses byte classes plus DFA transitions to test whether fewer width-specific branches help; table lookup costs may offset any benefit.

retained: Replaced the width-specific scalar decoder with a compact DFA whose byte-class table distinguishes valid lead ranges, continuation subranges, and invalid bytes.
Retained an ASCII run-skip path; DFA states enforce continuation counts and the restricted second-byte ranges for E0, ED, F0, and F4.

model_reported.summary: Proposed a bounded, pure-scalar lead-directed decoder to test reduced table and state-transition work against the measured baseline.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: The implementation uses ordinary bounded C++ byte accesses and does not rely on a version-sensitive API, instruction, or compiler property.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Recorded the valid baseline's three-sample mean and distinguished it from this unmeasured proposal; also reported the prior incorrect variant without inferring its cause.

proposal.hypothesis: A lead-directed scalar decoder may reduce the per-byte table lookups and state-dependent transitions of the supplied DFA on mixed-width input by validating continuation bytes directly per code point, while retaining the ASCII-run fast path. This may instead lose from its lead-classification branches; controller measurement is needed.

retained: Replace the byte-class and DFA transition tables with direct lead-range classification and continuation-byte checks grouped by UTF-8 sequence length.
Retain the ASCII-run scan and validate E0/ED and F0/F4 boundary restrictions explicitly.
Check remaining input length before each continuation-byte read to preserve bounds and malformed-input rejection.
